title: Solutions Architect, EMEA
description:
ABOUT EXA

We raised a $250M Series C to build the search engine for AIs. Led by a16z, with existing investors Benchmark, Lightspeed, and YC doubling down, the round brings Exa's valuation to $2.2 billion.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Solutions Architects are the technical tip of the spear in Exa's presales motion. From the first call to the technical win, you're the person who shows prospects what Exa can do and proves it works for their use case. You partner with Account Executives on new accounts and new opportunities, and you're measured on technical wins, POC conversion, and pipeline velocity. You'll cover accounts across EMEA from our London office.

You'll run discovery with engineers and executives, build demos that land, design and run workshops and proofs of concept, and make the technical case for Exa against alternatives. When a deal needs specialist depth, you pull in our Forward Deployed Engineers. When a deal closes, you hand the customer off to them with everything they need to get to production fast. This is not a demo-only role. You are an engineer who sells.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Lead the technical side of new opportunities alongside Account Executives, from first call through technical win

- Run discovery to understand a prospect's use case, architecture, data needs, and success criteria, and qualify where Exa fits

- Build and deliver tailored demos, sample apps, and prototypes that show what Exa can do on the prospect's own problem

- Design and run workshops and POCs with clear success criteria, timelines, and evaluation plans, then drive them to a decision

- Win technical evaluations by benchmarking Exa on quality, latency, and cost, and making a clear case against alternatives

- Handle technical objections and answer security, compliance, and architecture questions

- Bring in Forward Deployed Engineers as specialists when a deal needs deeper expertise, and run a clean handoff to them after close

- Build reusable pre-sales assets such as demo environments, reference architectures, and evaluation playbooks

- Several years of hands-on programming experience. You can build compelling demos, implement POCs end to end, and design and run rigorous evals in head-to-head competitive scenarios

- 2+ years of hands-on presales or technical sales experience, ideally at an AI-native or developer-first company. You've owned the technical side of deals, run discovery and demos with technical buyers, and helped carry opportunities to close

- Strong communication skills: you can adapt your pitch to CTOs, engineers, and PMs alike, and explain complex technology simply

- Track record of high performance in demanding environments, whether that's a top CS program, a competitive sport, a startup, or something else entirely

- High tolerance for context-switching, ambiguity, and sustained intensity

- Willingness to travel as needed for customer meetings and workshops

YOU MIGHT EXCEL IF YOU...

- Have worked as a solutions architect, solutions engineer, or sales engineer at a developer-tools, API, or AI company

- Have built with LLMs, RAG, or agents and can talk credibly about retrieval and search quality

- Have helped close revenue or driven commercial outcomes at a previous company

- Thrive in early-stage environments where your job description changes monthly

title: Developer Relations Engineer
description:
Thank you for considering Tailscale. If this job description resonates with you, please apply.  Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic!

About Tailscale 

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role

Tailscale is looking for a Developer Relations Engineer to own and improve the developer experience across Tailscale’s expanding product portfolio. You’ll help developers understand, adopt, extend, and build with our core VPN/connectivity product, while also shaping how that experience evolves as Tailscale expands into new product areas like secure AI access (Aperture), privileged access management (PAM), and whatever comes next.

You’re a builder, investigator, and storyteller. You write code, chase technical curiosities all the way down, and turn what you learn into things other developers can use like demos, docs, talks, blog posts, sample apps, workshops, videos, tools, and open source contributions. You build things, break things, explain things, and keep going until the thing you’re working on has a name.

You’re comfortable speaking at conferences and just as comfortable digging through an API, a GitHub issue, or a weird networking edge case until it makes sense. You’re probably the kind of person who runs a local AI model in your homelab and can explain exactly why. You ask “why does it work that way?” often, and your instinct is to make the answer clearer, simpler, and better for the next developer.

Requirements 

• Strong software engineering fundamentals, with demonstrated experience building, debugging, and shipping real projects through professional work, open source, self-directed learning, or ambitious personal projects.

• Ability to create clear, useful developer-facing materials, including code samples, demos, tutorials, docs, blog posts, videos, talks, and workshops.

• Deep curiosity about how systems work, especially across networking, infrastructure, security, identity, cloud, open source, AI, or developer tooling.

• A track record of building and explaining technical systems, such as production software, developer tools, infrastructure projects, homelabs, local AI setups, networking experiments, or open source contributions.

• Excellent written, verbal, and visual communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical ideas clearly, creatively, and practically.

• Experience presenting to technical audiences, whether through conferences, meetups, livestreams, workshops, podcasts, videos, or internal engineering forums.

• Comfortable working in public through GitHub issues, pull requests, community forums, social channels, open source projects, and developer feedback loops.

• Strong developer empathy, emotional intelligence, and product sense; you notice friction, understand why it matters, and help translate it into better docs, APIs, examples, workflows, and product experiences.

• Ability to work cross-functionally with engineering, product, marketing, support, community, and other technical stakeholders while operating independently and driving high-impact projects from idea to execution.

• Comfortable managing multiple workstreams, meeting regular publishing, event, or launch deadlines, discussing technical tradeoffs in detail, and traveling for events, conferences, and community moments.
